settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: doIntercept sets ReflectionContextState DENY_METHOD_EXECUTION=true, CREATE_NULL_OBJECTS=true and REPORT_CONVERSION_ERRORS=true around binding (lines 216-218), blocking method invocation such as foo.getBar() / @java.lang.Runtime@... style calls in normal mode.
acceptableName() requires the name to pass BOTH the excluded-pattern check and the accepted-pattern whitelist and the 100-char length limit (lines 412-418, 420-435).

DefaultAcceptedPatternsChecker default whitelist is restrictive, and DefaultExcludedPatternsChecker blocks class, session, request, application, context, parameters, _memberAccess, struts, dojo references (DefaultExcludedPatternsChecker.java lines 18-29).
Only RuntimeException during setParameter is swallowed (lines 302-309); other failures propagate.
candidates.description: ParametersInterceptor.doIntercept reads the request parameter map (attacker-controlled keys and values) and, for each accepted name, invokes newStack.setParameter(name, value), which compiles/evaluates the name as an OGNL expression against the action ValueStack. Acceptance is decided by isAcceptableParameter -> acceptableName(name) = isWithinLengthLimit(name) && !isExcluded(name) && isAccepted(name), plus an optional action-provided ParameterNameAware. isAccepted uses DefaultAcceptedPatternsChecker whose single default regex is broad; isExcluded uses DefaultExcludedPatternsChecker whose defaults are a 10-entry regex blacklist. Blacklist-style filtering of OGNL expressions is inherently bypass-prone, so if a parameter name/expression can be crafted that does not match any excluded pattern and does match the accepted pattern, it reaches OGNL evaluation. This is a candidate for OGNL-expression injection; the actual exploitability depends on OGNL version behavior and is not demonstrated in reviewed source.
missing_evidence: No end-to-end proof that the default accepted regex plus the excluded blacklist can be bypassed on this exact OGNL/Javassist version.
The bundled OGNL library version and its parse-time behaviors were not inspected.
Whether any deployed action in this repo widens the patterns (setAcceptParamNames/setExcludeParams or struts.xml params overrides) was not established for a concrete deployment.
preconditions: A Struts2 action is reachable whose interceptor stack includes the params (ParametersInterceptor) interceptor (the default stack does).
The attacker can supply HTTP request parameters whose names are used as OGNL property paths.
The excluded-pattern blacklist and accepted-pattern whitelist do not cover the crafted expression (defaults shipped in this snapshot).
candidates.title: Request parameter binding in ParametersInterceptor exposes OGNL evaluation of attacker-controlled parameter names, guarded only by configurable regex whitelists/blacklists

counter_evidence: The setter logs a WARN that overriding affects safety of the application (lines 40-41), signaling intended admin-only use.
An analogous ADDITIONAL_EXCLUDED_PATTERNS path exists to extend rather than replace, so replacement is a deliberate option.
Override requires configuration access; not reachable from HTTP request parameters in reviewed source.
candidates.description: DefaultExcludedPatternsChecker exposes setOverrideExcludePatterns annotated @Inject(value=XWorkConstants.OVERRIDE_EXCLUDED_PATTERNS, required=false). When the override property is set, the constructor-installed default blacklist (setExcludedPatterns(EXCLUDED_PATTERNS)) is replaced entirely with the operator-provided patterns (excludedPatterns = new HashSet<Pattern>() then compiled from the override). An erroneously minimal override (or empty value) therefore silently strips protections that exclude class/session/request/context/_memberAccess references from the global parameter filtering. This is a configuration-dependent defense-in-depth weakening: it depends on how the instance property is set (e.g. via system property / struts.properties) and by whom, so it is a candidate, not a proven vulnerability.
missing_evidence: Whether any config in this repository actually sets a weak/empty override value.
Whether these settings are reachable via request-driven configuration reload in this snapshot.
preconditions: Deployment sets XWorkConstants.OVERRIDE_EXCLUDED_PATTERNS (e.g. struts.excludedPatterns.* style override) to a value that omits critical patterns, or an attacker-influenceable config path sets it.
ParametersInterceptor is in the active stack.
candidates.title: Global exclusion of OGNL patterns can be fully replaced at startup via override config, removing default blacklist protections

counter_evidence: Setter emits a WARN about affecting application safety (lines 30-32).
ADDITIONAL_ACCEPTED_PATTERNS exists to extend the whitelist without replacing it.
Requires configuration privilege, not HTTP parameters, to trigger in reviewed source.
candidates.description: DefaultAcceptedPatternsChecker likewise exposes setOverrideAcceptedPatterns (@Inject value XWorkConstants.OVERRIDE_ACCEPTED_PATTERNS, required=false) which clears the default single whitelist regex and installs the operator-provided patterns. A loose override (e.g. an over-permissive pattern or empty set) reduces the whitelist that ParametersInterceptor relies on (via isAccepted) to decide which parameter names may be OGNL-evaluated. Combined with the blacklist this is the only name-screening before ValueStack.setParameter. This is a configuration-dependent candidate; it is not demonstrated to be attacker-reachable.
missing_evidence: No repository config found that sets a weak override value.
Impact on a concrete action stack not traced end-to-end.
preconditions: Deployment sets XWorkConstants.OVERRIDE_ACCEPTED_PATTERNS to an over-permissive or empty value.
candidates.title: Global accepted-pattern whitelist can be fully replaced at startup via override config, weakening parameter-name whitelisting

counter_evidence: Code uses short-circuit AND: acceptableName(name) && (parameterNameAware == null || parameterNameAware.acceptableParameterName(name)) — FALSE from acceptableName cannot be rescued by the action (line 342).
No action in reviewed apps overrides this in a way shown to re-enable an excluded name.
candidates.description: ParametersInterceptor.isAcceptableParameter accepts a name when acceptableName(name) is true AND (action is not ParameterNameAware OR action.acceptableParameterName(name) is true) — note this is an AND, so an action cannot accept a name the interceptor rejected; however the class Javadoc (lines 113-120) warns that ParameterNameAware acceptableParameterName 'takes precedence over ParametersInterceptor', which suggests historical/edge behavior where an action could re-enable excluded names. In this snapshot the boolean composition appears to keep the interceptor as the outer gate, so the documented precedence is not borne out by the code as written. Reported as a candidate only because the security-relevant contract and its documentation diverge.
missing_evidence: No concrete action implementing ParameterNameAware permissively was traced.
Documentation-vs-code mismatch is not itself an exploitable path without a permissive action.
preconditions: An action implements ParameterNameAware with a permissive acceptableParameterName.
Deployment relies on the Javadoc-described precedence semantics.
candidates.title: ParameterNameAware on the action can override the interceptor's excluded-name decision (documented precedence)
